questions.learning_material_text: Сначала прочитайте вопрос и выделите в нём ключевые слова. Затем найдите в тексте соответствующий фрагмент и сверяйте смысл, а не только совпадение отдельных слов: автор может использовать перефразировку.
questions.title: Задание 9
questions.prompt:
Вы проводите информационный поиск в ходе выполнения проектной работы. Определите, в каком из текстов A — F содержатся ответы на интересующие Вас вопросы 1 — 7 . Один из вопросов останется без ответа. Занесите Ваши ответы в таблицу .
1. What role will devices play in shopping?
2. What advantages has the new way of paying ?
3. How can shoppers order the food now?
4. Why the grocery shopping needs changes?
5. What new function will the stores perform?
6. How shopping of today is similar and different from the past?
7. How robots will help people in stores?
A. Grocery shopping has always been a necessity, but the way it’s been done hasn’t changed in decades. The stores may have gotten bigger, but the concepts were still the same: customers came into the store, picked their items, waited in line and took them home. But the changes in the grocery space are only just beginning and within the next five years, we’ll see great improvements to the convenience and overall experience of grocery shopping.
B. Customers will soon have more freedom to shop the store for the items they want and then simply walk out without having to wait in line because of cashierless retail, which comes into fashion. Some stores will take it a step further by picking out the items or having them delivered after so that customers aren’t weighed down with bags. Cashierless retail also frees up human employees to focus on assisting customers, keeping the store clean and providing a personalized customer experience.
C. Grocery stores will focus more on experiences and less on products. Instead of only being a place to purchase food, grocery stores will compete more on overall experience and aim to be a place where people can connect. Stores will feature more services and experiences, such as cooking classes and product demonstrations. Customers will come to experience all the store has to offer and also get their groceries instead of just coming for the products.
D. Customers are already used to receiving personalized offers and recommendations from many other companies, and it will soon come to grocery. By integrating smart devices, customers will be able to create a shopping list that can be automatically shared with the grocery store for real-time personalization. Personal prices with digital shelves will allow the stores to change prices in real time and also display promotions and dietary information.
E. The future of grocery shopping will be filled with as much AI and automation as possible. In stores, AI will take the form of robots going around the store to assist customers and track stock. Robots will be used to fulfill orders and make deliveries as well as to stock the shelves. AI and automation will allow customers to get exactly what they want right when they want it without having to waste time on unnecessary steps or items.
F. It used to be that customers had no other choice than to visit the grocery store and shop for items themselves, but nowadays nearly every grocery chain already has pick-up and delivery options, which will continue to develop in coming years. Shoppers will have the option to order their groceries online, through a mobile app or with voice commands and then pick up their orders in the store or hav e it delivered to the doorstep.
В ответ запишите цифры в последовательности A-F через запятую без пробелов.
Введите последовательность цифр без пробелов.

questions.title: Задание 10
questions.prompt:
Прочитайте текст. Определите, какие из приведённых утверждений 13 – 19 соответствуют содержанию текста (1 — True ), какие не соответствуют (2 — False ) и о чём в тексте не сказано, то есть на основании текста нельзя дать ни положительного, ни отрицательного ответа (3 — Not stated ). Запишите в поле ответа цифру 1, 2 или 3, соответствующую выбранному Вами варианту ответа.
The history of cricket
Cricket may have been invented during Saxon or Norman times by children living in the Weald, an area of dense woodlands and clearings in south-east England. The first reference to cricket being played as an adult sport was in 1611, and in the same year, a dictionary defined cricket as a boys' game. There is also the thought that cricket may have derived from bowls, by the intervention of a batsman trying to stop the ball from reaching its target by hitting it away.
Village cricket had developed by the middle of the 17th century and the first English “county teams” were formed in the second half of the century, as “local experts” from village cricket were employed as the earliest professionals. The first known game in which the teams use county names is in 1709.
In the first half of the 18th Century cricket established itself as a leading sport in London and the south-eastern counties of England. Its spread was limited by travel, but it was slowly gaining popularity in other parts of England and Women’s Cricket dates back to the 1745 , when the first known match was played in Surrey.
Cricket was introduced to North America via the English colonies as early as the 17th century, and in the 18th century it arrived in other parts of the globe. It was introduced to the West Indies by colonists and to India by British East India Company mariners. It arrived in Australia almost as soon as colonisation began in 1788 and the sport reached New Zealand and South Africa in the early years of the 19th century.
Cricket came to India around 1721 when British sailors reached the coast of Kutch. The first recorded cricket match in India happened in 1751. British army officers played against British settlers of the country. Indians were always part of the spectators in all these matches. As more Indian soldiers started taking on the sport, the Britishers started playing with their subordinates. This led to the first cricket club in Calcutta in 1792.
By 1877, Europeans had invited the Indians to play matches with them. This was followed by other powerful Indian communities as well. Upon seeing the talent and the potential of Indians, few players were made to represent the British team; the most prominent player was the Maharaja of Nawanagar , Ranjitsinhji , who was lauded for his performance by the Britishers.
As a very accessible sport, Cricket can be seen being played everywhere in the country. It is not uncommon to see children playing with a plank of wood as a bat even. As an established sport, cricket has its own exercises, drills and tips and techniques to bat, bowl and field better. Cricket is also an easier way to keep fit and be in shape than cultivating a workout habit.

1) True; 2) False; 3) Not stated;
14. The first time when teams used county names was in 1709 .
1) True; 2) False; 3) Not stated;
15. Women were as successful cricket players as men .
1) True; 2) False; 3) Not stated;
16. The first British colony that cricket reached was Australi a .
1) True; 2) False; 3) Not stated;
17. At first Indians only watches the game and didn’t play .
1) True; 2) False; 3) Not stated;
18. The Britishers did not allow Indians to play cricket with them until the 19th century .
1) True; 2) False; 3) Not stated;
19. Playing cricket doesn’t require physical strength .
1) True; 2) False; 3) Not stated;
